target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures detail the company's engineering capabilities and human capital structure. Specifically, both state that the company has assembled a large team of semiconductor and software design engineers globally and maintains design and development resources in the U.S., Asia, Europe, and Israel. The 2024 version (D002) includes the historical lineage context in S002, but the core matching topic of engineering resource distribution is supported by S003 and S004.

Both disclosures serve as the primary business overview, explicitly stating the company is a 'global technology leader' that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions. The 2023 version cites a 50-year history, while the 2024 version cites a 60-year history. These correspond to the same specific business identity and mission statement topic within Item 1.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD develops world-class software stacks, including tools, compilers, and drivers, and works with customers to define customized solutions using its IP and design leadership.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD emphasize the development of software stacks and tools as integral to their hardware engineering capabilities. AVGO discloses having a large team of 'semiconductor and software design engineers' with resources globally, highlighting the breadth of its engineering depth. AMD similarly focuses on 'world-class software stacks' including development tools and compilers, and explicitly mentions working with customers to define 'customized solutions' using its IP and design leadership, mirroring AVGO's integration of software expertise with its hardware portfolio.

We maintain design, product and software development engineering resources at locations in the U.S., Asia, Europe and Israel, providing us with engineering expertise worldwide.
We develop world-class software stacks that are used to enable our high-performance products.
Our software stacks include development tools, compilers, and drivers for our CPUs, APUs, GPUs and FPGAs.
We work closely with our customers to define and develop customized solutions to precisely match their requirements.

INTC describes its strategy as fostering an inclusive workplace where 'the world's best engineers' can fulfill their dreams, indicating a shared reliance on high-quality engineering talent distributed globally, even if INTC focuses more on culture and AVGO on geographic presence.

comparisons.peer_topic: Talent Development and Employee Engagement Initiatives
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel invests in talent development through training programs, rotational assignments, updated job architecture, mentoring, and employee resource groups. Employee perceptions are gathered via annual surveys, and a portion of executive and employee performance bonuses is linked to improvements in employee experience survey results.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and INTC both highlight investment in human capital and talent development as part of their operational strategy. AVGO notes its history of innovation and assembling a large team of engineers. INGO details specific investments in talent development, including 'training programs', 'rotational assignments', and 'mentoring', linking employee experience to performance bonuses. While AVGO focuses on the aggregate size and location of its engineering team, INTC provides specifics on how it develops and retains that talent, both serving the same underlying business need for skilled engineering resources.

sentences.text: Over the years, we have assembled a large team of semiconductor and software design engineers around the world.
We invest resources to develop the talent needed to remain at the forefront of innovation and make Intel an employer of choice.

We offer training programs and provide rotational assignment opportunities and have updated our job architecture to help employees create custom learning curricula for building skills and owning their careers.

Through our annual employee experience survey, employee inclusion survey, and manager development feedback survey, employees can voice their perceptions of the company, their managers, their work experiences, and their learning and development opportunities.
